clue.text: It's a gateway to the East, Charlie

definitions.text: It's a gateway to the East, Charlie

parts.words: It's a gateway to the East, Charlie
parts.note: the famous Berlin crossing between the American and Soviet sectors was named with the NATO alphabet word Charlie, so the answer is the first half of its name

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend called Charlie that this is the way into the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Checkpoint Charlie was the best-known crossing point in the Berlin Wall from West to East Berlin. The clue's 'Charlie' reads like someone being spoken to, but it is the rest of the crossing's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarded border crossing is a place where travellers are stopped and inspected before passing.

clue.text: Wild prophet docked shakily with this vessel

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, telling the solver the letters run in no fixed order
something done shakily is unsteady and jumbled, a second sign the letters get mixed
a docked tail is cut short, so the word prophet loses its last letter

explanation.surface: An unhinged prophet moors his boat unsteadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the T off PROPHET to leave PROPHE, and 'Wild' and 'shakily' both say to rearrange those six letters. 'docked' and 'vessel' paint a harbour scene, but docked means cut short here.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopper is a barge or container used to carry dredged mud or other loose material, so it counts as a vessel.

clue.text: Many a sailor has to perform in a downpour

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
tar is an old word for a seaman
to act is to perform on stage

explanation.surface: Lots of sailors have to do their duties out in pouring rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many a sailor' reads as one phrase about seamen, but it splits into C (a hundred, so many), A and TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract can mean a violent rush of water, including a heavy torrent of rain.

clue.text: Types of table-ware in the window

parts.note: a plate is one kind of tableware
a glass is another kind of tableware

explanation.surface: Different kinds of crockery are on display in a shop window.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Types' supplies two pieces of tableware in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Large sheets of thick polished glass of this kind are used to glaze shop windows.

clue.text: I do Bach so badly, the glory is gone

indicators.note: playing music badly mangles it, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A performer admits to murdering Bach so thoroughly that all splendour has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel the child Ichabod is named with a Hebrew phrase taken to mean 'the glory has departed'; the name is still used as a lament for lost splendour.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical name is glossed as an exclamation that splendour has departed, so it stands for the whole phrase.

clue.text: No transport of joy for clock-watchers

definitions.text: No transport of joy for clock-watchers

parts.words: No transport of joy for clock-watchers
parts.note: the passengers in this hired car anxiously watch the meter tick up the fare, so the ride is no delight

explanation.surface: Office workers waiting for home time find nothing that carries them away in rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport of joy' sounds like ecstasy and 'clock-watchers' like idle employees; read literally, it is a vehicle whose riders keep their eyes on the meter, the 'clock'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab charges by a meter, which passengers nervously watch as the fare climbs.

clue.text: Instruct wrongly so as to befog everyone ?

parts.note: to mist something is to cloud or befog it
each means every one individually

explanation.surface: A bad teacher wonders whether to confuse all the pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix mis- means badly, so to teach someone badly is to give them wrong instruction.

clue.text: He propounded world revolution

parts.note: the world here is the Earth, and its revolution is its orbit round the Sun, which this astronomer argued for

explanation.surface: A political radical preached a global uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Marxist calling for world revolution; the 16th-century Polish astronomer instead proposed that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish astronomer set out the heliocentric model in which the Earth orbits the Sun.

clue.text: A fair specimen makes a pound in the ring

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A good-looking competitor earns a pound in the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests boxing, but it is just the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: An albino is a creature lacking pigment, so its skin and hair are very pale.

clue.text: Place money ?

parts.note: a spot is a place
cash is money

explanation.surface: A two-word instruction to put money down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a definition: payment made on the spot is money paid at once.
explanation.definitionFit: This is payment made immediately on purchase, money handed over on the spot.

clue.text: Cordial drink ? Strangely enough it's eaten !

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of its normal order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised that a liqueur is eaten rather than drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like it means friendly, but a cordial is a sweet liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur, and cordial is an old name for such a drink.

clue.text: Female of the Species in major star role

definitions.text: Female of the Species in major star role

parts.words: Female of the Species in major star role
parts.note: the Latin word for a she-bear is the first half of the name of the Great Bear constellation

explanation.surface: An actress lands the leading part in a production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major star role' sounds like a theatre lead; it is the constellation Ursa Major, the Great Bear, and in Latin the word means she-bear.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin the word means a she-bear, and it begins the names of the Great and Little Bear constellations.

clue.text: Not worried messing up the double turn

indicators.note: messing something up throws it into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer is unbothered about fluffing a double pirouette.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone free from trouble has nothing to be anxious about.

clue.text: Does it consist of rolling or pedigree stock ?

definitions.text: Does it consist of rolling or pedigree stock ?

parts.words: Does it consist of rolling or pedigree stock ?
parts.note: split one way the letters name a freight train made of railway wagons, rolling stock; split another they name a fine bloodline, pedigree stock

explanation.surface: A question about whether a herd is made of railway wagons or prize cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: The same ten letters split as GOODS TRAIN, a freight train (rolling stock), and GOOD STRAIN, a fine breeding line (pedigree stock).
explanation.definitionFit: A fine line of breeding is the mark of pedigree livestock.

clue.text: Proverbial precedent for early closing legislation ?

definitions.text: Proverbial precedent for early closing legislation ?

parts.words: Proverbial precedent for early closing legislation ?
parts.note: the proverb mocks locking up after the horse has bolted, too late; the clue turns that into a joke about laws on shops closing early

explanation.surface: A question about what precedent lies behind laws making shops shut early.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'to shut the stable door after the horse has bolted'. 'Early closing' was the British half-day when shops shut; here the closing comes too late, not early.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb about shutting this barn entrance once the horse has bolted is the classic image of a belated precaution.

clue.text: Carroll's bat flew like one

parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Hatter sings that the little bat flies up above the world like a serving tray in the sky

explanation.surface: A remark on how a bat in a Lewis Carroll book flew.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hatter's parody runs 'Twinkle, twinkle, little bat ... Up above the world you fly, Like a tea-tray in the sky.'
explanation.definitionFit: The Hatter's song compares the flying bat to a flat board for carrying cups.

clue.text: Went against this clue's direction

parts.note: this is a Down clue, so going against its direction means moving upward

explanation.surface: Someone disobeyed the instructions given in this clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a Down entry, so going the opposite way is going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against a downward direction is to climb or rise.

clue.text: Vehicle returns with style to such revelry

definitions.note: the clue names the revelry, but the answer is the adjective describing it

indicators.note: a vehicle that returns goes back the way it came, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle for hire
chic is stylish elegance

explanation.surface: A car comes back in fine style to a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns CAB into BAC. The definition is a noun, but 'such revelry' is revelry of this kind, so the answer fills it as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus was the Roman god of wine, and riotous drunken merrymaking is named after him.

clue.text: "Love-thoughts lie rich when - - with bowers "(T Night)

definitions.text: "Love-thoughts lie rich when - - with bowers "(T Night)

parts.words: "Love-thoughts lie rich when - - with bowers "(T Night)
parts.note: the missing word completes Orsino's line at the end of the first scene of Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: A line of Shakespeare quoted with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Orsino ends Act 1 Scene 1 of Twelfth Night with 'Love-thoughts lie rich when canopied with bowers.'
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means covered overhead, as by a leafy arbour.

clue.text: Virginia doing a Uriah Heep ?

definitions.meaning: Virginia stands for the climbing plant that names itself after that state
Uriah Heep, in Dickens's David Copperfield, is a fawning, servile toady

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia behaves like Dickens's oily villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia creeper is a climbing plant; Uriah Heep in David Copperfield is the classic grovelling sycophant, a crawler.
explanation.definitionFit: The climbing plant grows along walls, and a sycophant is said to creep up to the powerful.

clue.text: There's a short, clear outcome from this score

definitions.note: the clue names the score, but the answer is the adjective describing such a score

indicators.note: the result coming out of these words is a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A brief, lucid result comes from this piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'a score of this kind', so the answer fills it as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A score written for a full band of strings, wind, brass and percussion is a symphonic one.

clue.text: Loch Jutland ?

definitions.meaning: the famous Scottish loch said to hold a monster
Jutland is a peninsula, and the question mark says it is an example of a headland

explanation.surface: A two-word question pairing a Scottish lake with a Danish peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Ness is the Scottish lake of monster fame; a ness is also a headland or promontory, which Jutland, the Danish peninsula, is a large example of.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Scottish lake and a promontory, and Jutland is a great promontory.

clue.text: He's more useful preparing the course than on it !

definitions.text: He's more useful preparing the course than on it !

parts.words: He's more useful preparing the course than on it !
parts.note: the course is first a meal course, carved in the kitchen, and second a golf course, where this kind of player sends the ball curving off line

explanation.surface: A remark about a groundsman who is better at preparing the track than racing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In the kitchen a slicer cuts food for a course of a meal; on a golf course a slicer is a player whose shots curve badly away.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting tool helps prepare a meal, while a golfer with a sliced shot goes astray on the links.

clue.text: It's a living

parts.note: a living is also a church post with a guaranteed income

explanation.surface: A shrug about a job that pays the bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a living' is what people say of an unexciting job, but a 'living' is also a Church of England post with its income.
explanation.definitionFit: A church office carrying an income for its parson is called a living.

clue.text: Irons on this date for the cavalry

definitions.text: Irons on this date for the cavalry

parts.words: Irons on this date for the cavalry
parts.note: put the clue's word Irons in front of a Roman date and you get the nickname of Cromwell's horsemen

explanation.surface: Horses are to be shod on a particular day.
explanation.walkthrough: IRONS + IDES (a Roman calendar date, as in the Ides of March) makes IRONSIDES, the nickname of Cromwell's cavalry in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar this was the middle day of a month, the fifteenth or thirteenth.

clue.text: District where the vine crop is ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A region where the grape harvest has failed.
explanation.definitionFit: A province is an administrative region of a country.

clue.text: For example, service engineers retreat then reappear

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers

explanation.surface: Army engineers fall back and then turn up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns EGREME into EMERGE. REME is a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out again into view is to resurface or come forth.

clue.text: They take their crests on board

definitions.text: They take their crests on board

parts.words: They take their crests on board
parts.note: the crests are the tops of waves, ridden while standing on a board

explanation.surface: Nobles carry their heraldic badges on to a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crests' and 'on board' suggest coats of arms on a ship, but the crests are wave tops and the board is a surfboard.
explanation.definitionFit: These sportspeople ride breaking waves standing on boards.
